sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. A c. 120-item wordlist of the 'Bumbarra tribe' (Port Denison to Cape Gloucester, inland to the head of the Proserpine River) in English amateur spelling (rooa 'kangaroo', koolachu 'opossum', goondooloo 'emu', githa 'war-spear', yamba 'camp'); no accent marks (checked on the page image at 110 dpi), and Curr's two pages of prose (pp. 4-5) discuss customs and a few lexical mergers, not pronunciation. This is the only primary record of Giya (AUSTLANG: 'all that remains for this language', citing Terrill 1998:87).
